sections.title: The Dodo's Story
poem_lines: Long ago, upon an island green,
Lived a bird unlike any ever seen.
The Dodo was gentle, large, and round,
With little wings and feet on the ground.
It could not fly across the sky,
Nor spread its wings and soar up high.
It ate fallen fruits beneath the trees,
And wandered freely in the gentle breeze.
Then sailors came across the sea,
Dogs, cats, and guns arrived one day,
While forests were cleared and taken away.
The last Dodo vanished in sixteen eighty-one,
And never again would it greet the morning sun.
Its story teaches us to care for every living thing,
And protect the precious life that nature brings.

questions.prompt: The poem says, ‘forests were cleared and taken away.’ Why would this have been harmful to the Dodo?
Do you think the disappearance of the Dodo was only the result of hunting? What other human actions contributed to its extinction?
Can you think of a living species today that may face threats because of human activities? What could people do to protect it?
If you could change one event in the Dodo's story, what would you change and why?
